subject: Physics
subtopic: Work Done by a Variable Force
stem: A particle of mass M moves along a horizontal x axis from \(x=0\) to \(x=L\). The coefficient of kinetic friction varies as a function of x as \(\mu_k(x) = \mu_0 - \alpha x\), where \(\mu_0\), \(\alpha\) are constants of appropriate dimensions, so that \(\mu_k(L)=0\). The total work done by the frictional force during the motion is \(n\mu_0 MgL\), where g is the acceleration due to gravity. The value of n is :
solution: \(\mu_k = \mu_0 - \alpha x\); \(\mu_0 - \alpha L = 0 \Rightarrow \alpha = \dfrac{\mu_0}{L}\). W.D. by kinetic friction \(= \int f_k\,dx\cos 180^\circ = \int_0^L \mu_k mg\,dx(-1) = -\int_0^L (\mu_0 - \alpha x)mg\,dx = -\left[\mu_0 mgL - \alpha mg\dfrac{L^2}{2}\right] = -\left[\mu_0 mgL - \dfrac{\mu_0}{L}mg\dfrac{L^2}{2}\right] = -\left[\dfrac{\mu_0 mgL}{2}\right]\). On comparing magnitude with \(n\mu_0 mgL\), \(n = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

subject: Physics
stem: The mean free path of molecules in an ideal gas A is half that of another ideal gas B. The diameter of the spherical molecules of gas A is twice the diameter of the molecules of B. If number densities of the gases A and B are \(n_A\) and \(n_B\), respectively, then the correct option is :
solution: \(\lambda = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2}\dfrac{1}{n}\), so \(n \propto \dfrac{1}{\lambda d^2}\). \(\dfrac{n_A}{n_B} = \dfrac{\lambda_B}{\lambda_A}\times\left(\dfrac{d_B}{d_A}\right)^2 = 2\times\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\). Thus \(n_A = \dfrac{n_B}{2}\).

subject: Physics
stem: Two identical inductors are connected in two different configurations P and Q, where a time varying current \(I(t)\) is flowing, as shown in the figure. The induced emf between points a and b for configuration P is \(E_P\) and that for configuration Q is \(E_Q\). The ratio \(E_P/E_Q\) is : [Neglect the effect of mutual inductance.]
solution: \(E_P = \dfrac{L\,di}{dt}\). \(E_Q = L\dfrac{di/2}{dt} = \dfrac{L}{2}\dfrac{di}{dt}\). \(\dfrac{E_P}{E_Q} = \dfrac{L\,di/dt}{\frac{L}{2}\,di/dt} = 2\).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Harmonics in Open and Closed Pipes
stem: For sound waves, if the number of nodes for the \(5^{th}\) harmonic of an open-ended pipe is n and that for the \(9^{th}\) harmonic of the same pipe with one of its ends closed is m, the ratio \(\dfrac{n}{m}\) is :
solution: For COP and OOP, No. of nodes \(= m + 1\) where m = No. of overtone. In OOP, \(5^{th}\) harmonic means \(4^{th}\) OT, m = 4, so no. of nodes \(n = 4 + 1 = 5\). In COP, \(9^{th}\) harmonic means \(4^{th}\) OT means m = 4, then no of nodes \(= m + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5\). So ratio \(\dfrac{n}{m} = \dfrac{5}{5} = 1\).

subject: Physics
stem: Consider a long solenoid of length l and radius r. If n is the number of turns per unit length and \(\mu_0\) is the permeability of free space, the inductance of the solenoid is :
solution: \(L = n^2\mu_0 A l = n^2\mu_0\pi r^2 l\). Option (1).

subject: Physics
stem: Consider a particle moving along a straight line, whose position as a function of time is given by \(s(t) = \alpha t^2 - \beta t + \gamma\), where \(\alpha = 1\ \text{ms}^{-2}\), \(\beta = 6\ \text{ms}^{-1}\) and \(\gamma = 5\ \text{m}\). The average speed of the particle, in \(\text{ms}^{-1}\), from \(t = 0\) to \(t = 6\ \text{s}\) is :
solution: \(S = \alpha t^2 - \beta t + \gamma = t^2 - 6t + 5\). \(v = \dfrac{ds}{dt} = (2t - 6)\ \text{m/s}\). Distance travelled \(= |A_1| + |A_2| = 2\left[\dfrac{1}{2}\times 3\times 6\right] = 18\ \text{m}\). Average speed \(v_{avg} = \dfrac{\text{distance}}{\text{Time}} = \dfrac{18}{6} = 3\ \text{m/s}\).

subtopic: Photoelectric Effect - Photocurrent and Stopping Potential
stem: A beam of light falls on a metal surface such that photo-electrons are generated. If power of the light source starts to decrease linearly with time t, then variation of the photocurrent I and magnitude of the stopping potential \(|V|\) with time is best represented by :
options: I decreases linearly with t; \(|V|\) remains constant with t
I decreases linearly with t; \(|V|\) decreases linearly with t
I remains constant with t; \(|V|\) decreases linearly with t
I remains constant with t; \(|V|\) remains constant with t
solution: \(P = \dfrac{nhC}{\lambda} = nh\nu\). If power decreases then n decreases but frequency remains same as source is same. Photocurrent will decrease and stopping potential remains same.

subject: Physics
stem: Three identical capacitors P, Q and S, each of the capacitance C, are connected to a battery of voltage V, as shown in the figure. If the energy stored in the capacitor P and total energy stored in the system are \(U_P\) and \(U_T\), respectively, then the ratio \(\dfrac{U_P}{U_T}\) is :
solution: P and Q are in series (each gets \(\pm CV/2\)) and S in parallel gets \(\pm CV\). \(U_P = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{(CV/2)^2}{C} = \dfrac{1}{8}CV^2\). \(U_T = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{(CV/2)^2}{C} + \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{(CV/2)^2}{C} + \dfrac{1}{2}CV^2 = \dfrac{3}{4}CV^2\). \(\dfrac{U_P}{U_T} = \dfrac{\frac{1}{8}CV^2}{\frac{3}{4}CV^2} = \dfrac{1}{6}\).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Equation of Continuity and Bernoulli's Principle
stem: Water flows in a streamline motion through a horizontal pipe of circular cross-section as shown in the figure. The pressure difference of water between P and Q is \(15\ \text{Nm}^{-2}\). The area of cross-section at P and Q are \(40\ \text{cm}^2\) and \(20\ \text{cm}^2\), respectively. The rate of flow of water through the pipe, in \(\text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}\), is : [Take density of water \(= 1000\ \text{kg m}^{-3}\)]
solution: By continuity \(A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2 \Rightarrow 40 v_1 = 20 v_2 \Rightarrow v_2 = 2v_1\). By Bernoulli \(P_1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\rho v_1^2 = P_2 + \dfrac{1}{2}\rho v_2^2\), so \(P_1 - P_2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\rho[(2v_1)^2 - v_1^2]\), \(\dfrac{15\times 2}{10^3} = 3v_1^2\), \(v_1 = 0.1\ \text{m/s}\). Rate of flow \(\dfrac{dV}{dt} = A_1 v_1 = 40\times 10^{-4}\times 0.1 = 4\times 10^{-4}\ \text{m}^3/\text{s} = 4\times 10^{-4}\times 10^6\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s} = 400\ \text{cm}^3/\text{s}\).

subject: Physics
stem: In the measurement of viscosity of liquids using terminal velocity experiment, spherical balls of same radius but having different densities are used. The variation of the terminal velocity (v) with the ratio of density of spherical ball (\(\sigma\)) to density of the liquid (\(\rho\)), is best represented by :
options: Line with positive slope crossing the \(\sigma/\rho\) axis at 1 (v = 0 at \(\sigma/\rho = 1\), rising for \(\sigma/\rho > 1\)); no dotted extension below axis
Line with positive slope, dotted extension passing through origin, v positive at \(\sigma/\rho = 0\)
Line with positive slope, dotted extension below axis, meeting axis at \(\sigma/\rho = 1\)
solution: Given density of ball (solid) \(\rightarrow \sigma\), density of liquid \(\rightarrow \rho\). Terminal velocity \(v = \dfrac{2r^2}{9\eta}(\sigma - \rho)g = \dfrac{2r^2}{9\eta}\rho\left[\dfrac{\sigma}{\rho} - 1\right]g = \dfrac{2r^2\rho g}{9\eta}\left(\dfrac{\sigma}{\rho}\right) - \dfrac{2r^2\rho g}{9\eta}\). It's an equation of positive slope and negative straight line intercept. If \(\dfrac{\sigma}{\rho} = 1\) then \(v = 0\). So correct graph is (1).

subject: Physics
stem: Two planets \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) with equal mass have radii \(R_1\) and \(R_2\), respectively, where \(R_2 = \dfrac{R_1}{2}\). The escape speeds of \(P_1\) and \(P_2\) are \(v_1\) and \(v_2\), respectively. Then \(\dfrac{v_2}{v_1}\) is :
solution: \(V_{es} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}\). \(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{R_1}{R_2}} = \sqrt{2}\).

subject: Physics
stem: In a solar system, the time-period of revolution of a planet tracing a circular orbit of radius R is proportional to :
solution: By Kepler's III law, \(T^2 \propto R^3\), so \(T \propto R^{3/2}\).

subject: Physics
stem: Two infinitely long parallel conducting wires A and B carry currents I and 2I, respectively, in the same direction. The wire A has uniform mass per unit length \(\lambda\) and lies on an insulated floor. The wire B is kept fixed at a height h above the floor. The minimum magnitude of h so that the wire A does not rise from the floor is : [g is the acceleration due to gravity and \(\mu_0\) is the permeability of free space]
solution: At equilibrium \(F_m = W\). \(\dfrac{F_m}{\ell} = \dfrac{W}{\ell} = \dfrac{mg}{\ell} = \lambda g\). \(\dfrac{\mu_0(2I)(I)}{2\pi(h)} = \lambda g\). \(h = \dfrac{\mu_0 I^2}{\pi\lambda g}\).

subject: Physics
stem: An ideal Zener diode with breakdown voltage of \(-3\text{V}\) is reverse biased with a negative input voltage \(V_i = -5\text{V}\). The magnitude of voltage difference between points B and A is :
solution: Here Zener diode is in reverse biased so voltage drop across Zener diode is 3V. Voltage difference across points B and A: \(V_{BA} = 5 - 3 = 2\text{V}\).

subject: Physics
stem: In an adiabatic expansion, the temperature of one mole of an ideal monatomic gas (\(\gamma = 5/3\)) decreases from 60 K to 50 K. The work done by the gas in the process is : (Take the universal gas constant as \(R = 8.3\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\))
solution: \(W = \dfrac{\mu R\Delta T}{1 - \gamma} = \dfrac{1\times 8.3\times(-10)}{1 - \frac{5}{3}} = \dfrac{3\times 8.3\times 10}{2} = 124.5\ \text{J}\).

subject: Physics
chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
stem: A ray of light with wavelength \(\lambda\) is incident on three different photo-electric cells namely 1, 2 and 3. The threshold wavelength of these photo-electric cells are \(\lambda_1\), \(\lambda_2\) and \(\lambda_3\), respectively and the magnitude of stopping potentials of these cells are \(V_1\), \(V_2\) and \(V_3\), respectively. The relation between \(\lambda\) and threshold wavelengths are \(\lambda_1 < \lambda\), \(\lambda_2 > \lambda\) and \(\lambda_3 \gg \lambda\). The correct option is :
solution: For photo-electric effect wavelength of incident light should be less than threshold wavelength. (i) \(\lambda_1 < \lambda\), no photoelectric effect takes place. (ii) \(\lambda_2 > \lambda\), photoelectric effect takes place. (iii) \(\lambda_3 \gg \lambda\), photoelectric effect takes place. Frequency of 3 > frequency of 2, so \(V_3 > V_2\) and \(V_1 = 0\).

subject: Physics
chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
stem: A photon and an electron, each of 20 eV energy, move in free space. The ratio of linear momentum of electron \(p_e\) to that of photon \(p_{Ph}\), \(\dfrac{p_e}{p_{Ph}}\), is : (Take speed of light \(= 3\times 10^8\ \text{ms}^{-1}\), charge of electron \(= -1.6\times 10^{-19}\ \text{C}\) and mass of electron \(= 9\times 10^{-31}\ \text{kg}\))
solution: \(\dfrac{p_e}{p_{Ph}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2mE_e}}{E_{Ph}/C}\) with \(E_e = E_{Ph} = E\). \(\dfrac{p_e}{p_{Ph}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{E}}\times C = \sqrt{\dfrac{2\times 9\times 10^{-31}}{20\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}}}\times 3\times 10^8 = \dfrac{3}{4}\times 10^{-6}\times 3\times 10^8 = 225\).

subject: Physics
stem: Which of the following measurements require 'index correction'?
options: Measurement of resistance of a wire using meter bridge
Measurement of gravitational acceleration using simple pendulum
Measurement of focal length of lenses using optical bench
Measurement of speed of sound using resonance tube
solution: In an optical bench experiment, index correction also known as bench correction. Optical bench experiment performed to calculate focal length of lenses.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Potential Due to Uniformly Charged Sphere
stem: A unit positive point charge is taken slowly through an infinitesimally thin tube that is inside a charged dielectric sphere of radius R, having uniform positive charge density \(\rho\), as shown in the figure. The initial and final positions of the charge are marked by A and B at distances 2R and 3R respectively, from the centre of the sphere. In this process, the magnitude of the total work done on the point charge is \(\dfrac{\rho R^2}{n\epsilon_0}\). The value of n is : (\(\epsilon_0\) is the permittivity of vacuum)
solution: \(W = q\Delta V = q(V_B - V_A) = 1\left(\dfrac{kQ}{3R} - \dfrac{kQ}{2R}\right) = \dfrac{-kQ}{6R} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{\rho\times\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3}{6R} = \dfrac{\rho R^2}{18\epsilon_0}\). So \(n = 18\).

subject: Physics
stem: Consider three media P, Q and R with refractive indices 1, 1.25, and 1.5, respectively. The medium Q having a thickness of 5 cm is placed between extended media P and R as shown in the figure. An object O is placed at the centre of medium Q. If viewed from medium P near the normal direction, the apparent depth of O is \(h_1\). For similar observation from medium R, the apparent depth is \(h_2\). The value of \(|h_1 - h_2|\), in cm, is :
solution: For observer I: \(\dfrac{d'}{d} = \dfrac{\mu_2}{\mu_1}\), \(\dfrac{d'}{2.5} = \dfrac{1}{1.25}\), \(d' = 2\ \text{cm} = h_1\). For observer II: \(\dfrac{d'}{d} = \dfrac{\mu_2}{\mu_1}\), \(\dfrac{d'}{2.5} = \dfrac{1.5}{1.25}\), \(d' = 3\ \text{cm} = h_2\). \(|h_1 - h_2| = 1\ \text{cm}\).

subject: Physics
chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
stem: A frictionless circular wire of unit radius is fixed on the horizontal plane. Two point particles of unit mass start moving simultaneously from point \(A\left(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\) with identical uniform angular speeds in opposite directions, and meet again at point \(B\left(\theta = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\). During this time, which of the following figures schematically represent the magnitude of the total linear momentum P of the system, as a function of \(\theta\)?
options: P starts high, dips to zero at \(\theta = 0\), then rises (V-shape / cusp at 0)
P is zero at \(\theta = \pi/2\) and \(-\pi/2\), maximum at \(\theta = 0\) (dome shape)
P decreases linearly (straight line falling from \(\pi/2\) to \(-\pi/2\))
solution: \(\vec{P_1} + \vec{P_2} = mv\sin\theta\,\hat{i} - mv\cos\theta\,\hat{j} + (-mv\sin\theta\,\hat{i} - mv\cos\theta\,\hat{j})\). \(P_{Total} = |\vec{P_1} + \vec{P_2}| = 2mv\cos\theta\). At \(\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\), \(P_{Total} = 0\); at \(\theta = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), \(P_{Total} = 0\); at \(\theta = 0\), \(P_{Total\,max} = 2mV\). So graph is a dome (option 3).

subject: Physics
stem: The temperature of a metallic sphere of radius R is increased by a small amount \(\Delta T\). If the linear coefficient of thermal expansion of the metal is \(\alpha\), the approximate increase in the volume of the sphere is :
solution: \(\gamma = \dfrac{\Delta V}{V}\times\dfrac{1}{\Delta T}\), so \(3\alpha\Delta T\times V = \Delta V\). \(\Delta V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3\times 3\alpha\Delta T = 4\pi R^3\alpha\Delta T\).

subject: Physics
stem: A cylindrical cork of uniform density floats in a liquid of density \(\rho_1\). If the cork is depressed slightly and released, it oscillates harmonically with time period T. If the same cork floats in another liquid of density \(\rho_2\), then the similar oscillation has time period 2T. The value of \(\rho_2/\rho_1\) is :
solution: Force on cork when cross section area is A: \(F = -\rho gAx\). Compare with \(F = -kx\), \(k = \rho Ag\). \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{k}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{m}{\rho Ag}}\), so \(T \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\rho}}\). Now \(\dfrac{T_1}{T_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\rho_2}{\rho_1}}\), \(\dfrac{T}{2T} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\rho_2}{\rho_1}} \Rightarrow \dfrac{\rho_2}{\rho_1} = \dfrac{1}{4}\).

subject: Physics
stem: One main scale division of a Vernier calliper is equal to 1 mm and the number of divisions on the Vernier scale is 10. When both the jaws touch each other, the Vernier scale shifts to the left of zero of the main scale in such a way that \(4^{th}\) Vernier division coincides with a division of the main scale. If this Vernier calliper measures the length of a wire to be 1 cm, the actual length of the wire is :
solution: MSD = 1 mm, VSD = 0.9 mm, LC = 0.1 mm = 0.01 cm. \(ZE = -(\text{Total} - \text{coinciding VSD})\,LC = -(10 - 4)(0.01) = -0.06\ \text{cm}\). Actual reading = Measured reading \(-\) ZE = 1 cm \(- (-0.06)\) cm = 1.06 cm. (Bonus)

subject: Physics
stem: Consider a spring mass simple harmonic oscillator in one dimension. The mass of the particle is m kg and the spring constant is k \(\text{Nm}^{-1}\). At a given instant, the extension of the spring is x meter and the speed of the particle is v \(\text{ms}^{-1}\). On the x-v plane, if the graph of v as a function of x is a circle, then the correct option is :
solution: In a spring mass system, the total energy is \(E = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 + \dfrac{1}{2}kx^2\), or \(\dfrac{mv^2}{2E} + \dfrac{kx^2}{2E} = 1\), or \(\dfrac{v^2}{2E/m} + \dfrac{x^2}{2E/k} = 1\). Compare with \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2} + \dfrac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\). For circle \(a^2 = b^2 \Rightarrow \dfrac{2E}{m} = \dfrac{2E}{k} \Rightarrow m = k\).

subject: Physics
stem: The lens combination as shown in the figure, consists of two lenses, \(L_1\) and \(L_2\), of the focal lengths +10 cm and \(-10\) cm, respectively. The position of the image formed is :
options: 20 cm to the left of the concave lens
60 cm to the left of the concave lens
30 cm to the right of the concave lens
60 cm to the right of the concave lens
solution: 1st lens: \(u = -30\ \text{cm}\), \(f = 10\ \text{cm}\). \(v = \dfrac{uf}{u + f} = \dfrac{-30\times 10}{-30 + 10} = 15\ \text{cm}\). Image of first lens acts as a virtual object for second lens. 2nd lens: \(u = 12\ \text{cm}\), \(f = -10\ \text{cm}\). \(v = \dfrac{12\times(-10)}{12 - 10} = -60\ \text{cm}\) (virtual image). Negative sign indicates left of the concave lens.

subject: Physics
stem: An ac voltage \(V = 220\sin(2\times 10^3 t)\) Volt is applied to a series LCR circuit. Then the current amplitude in this circuit is : (Given : \(L = 10\ \text{mH}\), \(C = 25\ \mu\text{F}\), \(R = 100\ \Omega\))
solution: \(X_L = \omega L = 2\times 10^3\times 10\times 10^{-3} = 20\ \Omega\). \(X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{10^6}{2\times 10^3\times 25} = 20\ \Omega\). \(X_L = X_C\), hence LCR circuit is in resonance. So \(Z = R\); \(I_0 = \dfrac{V_0}{Z} = \dfrac{V_0}{R} = \dfrac{220}{100} = 2.2\ \text{Amp}\).

subject: Physics
chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
stem: A thin horizontal disc is rotating about a vertical axis passing through its fixed centre O. Its angular momentum is \(L_A\) and \(L_B\) computed about points A and B, respectively, with \(OB = 2\times OA\). The value of \(\dfrac{L_A}{L_B}\) is :
solution: For a pure rotation body \(L_{about any point} = I_{about which body rotating}\,\omega\). \(L_A = \dfrac{MR^2}{2}\omega \Rightarrow L_B = \dfrac{MR^2}{2}\omega\). \(\dfrac{L_A}{L_B} = 1\).

subject: Physics
stem: A conducting loop of finite resistance lies on the x-y plane. There is a constant magnetic field in the z direction. The area of the loop varies with time t, as \(A = A_0(1 + \sin t)\) in appropriate units. The figure that correctly indicates the qualitative behaviour of the power P dissipated in the loop as a function of time is :
options: Series of positive humps that touch zero periodically (like \(|\cos t|\) squared humps, both humps same height)
Curve starting high, dipping to zero once (single cusp), then rising
solution: \(\phi = BA = BA_0(1 + \sin t)\). \(e = \dfrac{-d\phi}{dt} = -BA_0\cos t \Rightarrow P = \dfrac{e^2}{R} = \dfrac{B^2 A_0^2\cos^2 t}{R}\). \(P \propto \cos^2 t\).

subject: Physics
subtopic: Field Due to Charge in Conductor Cavity
stem: A point charge Q is placed inside a cavity within a solid isolated conducting sphere. Consider points A, B and C as shown in the figure, where the magnitudes of the electric fields are \(E_A\), \(E_B\) and \(E_C\), respectively. The points B and C are at the same distance from the center of the solid sphere. The correct option is :
solution: \(E_A = \dfrac{kQ}{r^2} \neq 0\) (A is inside the cavity, field due to Q). \(E_B = \dfrac{kQ}{r_B^2} = \dfrac{kQ}{r_C^2} = E_C\) (outside the conductor, at equal distances from centre the induced charge distributes so the field is that of Q at the centre).

subject: Physics
stem: Consider a fixed uniformly charged insulating sphere with radius R and total charge +Q. A point charge \(-q\) (\(q \ll Q\)) with mass m is released from rest at a distance of 3R from the centre of the charged sphere. When the point charge reaches the surface of the sphere, its speed is : (\(\epsilon_0\) is the permittivity of vacuum, neglect gravitational forces).
solution: \(K_A + U_A = K_B + U_B\). \(-qV_A = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 + (-qV_B) \Rightarrow -\dfrac{KQq}{3R} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 - q\dfrac{KQ}{R}\). \(\dfrac{2}{3}\dfrac{KQq}{R} = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{\dfrac{Qq}{3\pi\epsilon_0 R m}}\).

subject: Physics
stem: In Geiger-Marsden experiment, the number of scattered \(\alpha\)-particles \(N(\theta)\) is plotted as a function of scattering angle \(\theta\). Which of the following options represents the correct plot?
options: \(N(\theta)\) increasing (rising straight line on log scale) from 0 to 180 degrees
\(N(\theta)\) nearly flat then falling off sharply toward 180 degrees
\(N(\theta)\) starting very high near small \(\theta\) and decreasing sharply, levelling off toward 180 degrees
\(N(\theta)\) low at ends, plateau high in the middle (trapezoidal)
solution: \(N \propto \dfrac{1}{\sin^4(\theta/2)}\).

subject: Physics
stem: Consider two circuits, (A) and (B), each having two resistors. One of them has a positive temperature coefficient of resistance, \(+\alpha\), while the other one has a negative temperature coefficient, \(-\alpha\), as shown in the figure. The current through these circuits are denoted by \(I_A\) and \(I_B\). At initial temperature, the resistance of the two resistors is \(R_0\). As the temperature is increased, the correct option that describes the variation of current in these circuits is : (In A the two resistors \(R_0(1-\alpha\Delta T)\) and \(R_0(1+\alpha\Delta T)\) are in series; in B they are in parallel.)
solution: \(R_A = R_1 + R_2 = R_0(1 + \alpha\Delta T) + R_0(1 - \alpha\Delta T) = 2R_0\). \(I_A = \dfrac{V}{R_A} = \dfrac{V}{2R_0}\), does not depend on temperature. \(R_B = \dfrac{R_1 R_2}{R_1 + R_2} = \dfrac{R_0^2(1 + \alpha\Delta t)(1 - \alpha\Delta t)}{R_0(1 + \alpha\Delta t) + R_0(1 - \alpha\Delta t)} = \dfrac{R_0^2(1 - \alpha^2\Delta t^2)}{2R_0} = \dfrac{R_0}{2}(1 - \alpha^2\Delta t^2)\). As \(\Delta t\uparrow\), \(R_B\downarrow\), \(I_B\uparrow\).

subject: Physics
stem: Consider that \(\sigma_S\), \(k_B\), b represent Stefan-Boltzmann constant, Boltzmann constant and Wien's displacement law constant, respectively. The dimension of \(\sigma_S k_B^{-1} b\) is :
solution: \([\sigma_S][k_B^{-1}][b] = \left[\dfrac{\text{Intensity}}{(\text{Temp})^4}\right]\left[\dfrac{\text{Energy}}{\text{Temp}}\right]^{-1}[\lambda_{max}\,\text{Temp}] = \left[\dfrac{MT^{-3}}{K^4}\right]\left[\dfrac{ML^2 T^{-2}}{K}\right]^{-1}[LK] = [M^0 L^{-1}T^{-1}K^{-2}]\).

subject: Physics
subtopic: EM Wave in a Dielectric Medium
stem: An electromagnetic wave travelling in a lossless dielectric medium having a dielectric constant \(\epsilon_r = 9\), has the electric field, \(E_x = E_0\sin(kz - 2\pi\times 10^6 t)\ \text{Vm}^{-1}\) where \(E_0\) is the amplitude and k is the wave vector. Among the following options, the incorrect choice is :
options: The speed of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium is \(10^8\ \text{ms}^{-1}\)
The wavelength of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium is 300 m
The magnetic field is given by the relation \(B_y = \dfrac{B_0}{v}\sin(kz - 2\pi\times 10^6 t)\) where v is the speed of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium
The direction of propagation of the electromagnetic wave is along \(+z\)
solution: Speed of EMW in a medium \(C_m = \dfrac{C}{\sqrt{\mu_r\epsilon_r}}\). Here \(\mu_r \approx 1\), \(\epsilon_r = 9\). \(C_m = \dfrac{C}{\sqrt{1\times 9}} = \dfrac{3\times 10^8}{3} = 10^8\ \text{m/sec}\) (Correct, option 1). (2) \(v = f\lambda \Rightarrow \lambda_m = \dfrac{C_m}{f}\). Here \(2\pi f = \omega = 2\pi\times 10^6 \Rightarrow f = 10^6\). \(\lambda_m = \dfrac{C_m}{f} = \dfrac{10^8}{10^6} = 100\ \text{m}\) (Incorrect, stated 300 m). (3) \(\dfrac{E_0}{B_0} = v \Rightarrow B_0 = \dfrac{E_0}{v}\); \(B_y = \dfrac{E_0}{v}\sin(kz - 2\pi\times 10^6 t)\), so the given relation with \(B_0/v\) is Incorrect. (4) EMW propagating in \(+z\) (correct). So incorrect statements are 2 and 3; the official key is (2).

subject: Physics
stem: Consider that an electron is revolving in an excited state of Hydrogen atom with velocity \(\sqrt{25.6}\times 10^5\ \text{ms}^{-1}\). The radius of the orbit is \(x\times 10^{-9}\ \text{m}\). The value of x is : [Take the mass of electron to be \(9\times 10^{-31}\ \text{kg}\), charge of electron \(= -1.6\times 10^{-19}\ \text{C}\) and \(\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} = 9\times 10^9\ \text{N m}^2\text{C}^{-2}\)]
solution: \(\dfrac{mv^2}{r} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{e^2}{r^2}\). \(\dfrac{9\times 10^{-31}\times 25.6\times 10^5\times 10^5}{r} = 9\times 10^9\times\dfrac{1.6\times 10^{-19}\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}}{r^2}\). \(r = \dfrac{256\times 10^{-40}}{256\times 10^4\times 10^5}\times\dfrac{10^9}{10^{-31}} = 1\times 10^{-9}\ \text{m} = x\times 10^{-9}\ \text{m}\). \(x = 1\).

subject: Physics
stem: A car travels on a circular racetrack of radius 50 m, which is banked at an angle \(\theta\). If the car travels at a speed \(10\ \text{ms}^{-1}\), then the wear and tear on its tyres is minimum. Taking the acceleration due to gravity to be \(10\ \text{ms}^{-2}\), the value of \(\theta\) is :
solution: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{V^2}{Rg} = \dfrac{(10)^2}{50\times 10} = \dfrac{1}{5}\). \(\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{5}\right)\).

subject: Physics
stem: Three identical p-n junction diodes \(D_1\), \(D_2\) and \(D_3\) are connected across a battery as shown in the figure. If the width of the depletion regions of \(D_1\), \(D_2\) and \(D_3\) are \(W_1\), \(W_2\) and \(W_3\), respectively, then the correct option is :
solution: Here diode \(D_1\) is F.B., diode \(D_2\) is unbias and diode \(D_3\) is R.B. In F.B width of depletion region decreases and in R.B width of depletion region increases so order of width of depletion region is \(W_3 > W_2 > W_1\).

stem:
The following table presents the part of the electromagnetic spectrum and their corresponding major applications.

| Part of the electromagnetic spectrum | | Applications |
|---|---|---|
| P Microwave | I | For purifying the water |
| Q UV rays | II | For warming the food |
| R Gamma rays | III | For AM and FM communication systems |
| S Radio wave | IV | For treating the Cancer cells |

The correct option is :
solution: Microwaves are used for warming the food (P-II). UV rays are used for purifying the water (Q-I). Gamma rays are used for treating the cancer cells (R-IV). Radio wave are used for AM and FM communication system (S-III). (From NCERT) Ans. P-II, Q-I, R-IV, S-III.

subject: Physics
stem: Bob B of mass m at rest is hanging vertically from the ceiling via a massless string of length 10 m, as shown in the figure. Point mass A of mass m travelling horizontally with speed \(10\ \text{ms}^{-1}\) hits bob B elastically. The bob B rises h meter after the collision. Taking the acceleration due to gravity \(g = 10\ \text{ms}^{-2}\) and neglecting the size of the bob, the value of h is :
solution: Mass same, collision head on elastic, velocity will interchange. After that by conservation of mechanical energy: \(\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 = mgh\), \(h = \dfrac{v^2}{2g} = \dfrac{100}{20} = 5\ \text{m}\).
